items.title: LTM: Latent Transition Based In-Context Memory for Vision-Language-Action Models

items.title: Choosing a Chunking Strategy for Your LLM Apps: A Decision-Tree Approach

items.title: Temporal Specification Guidance for Text-to-Video Generation
items.summary: This paper introduces Temporal Specification Guidance, a method using formal Temporal Logic to improve text-to-video generation models' ability to satisfy temporal requirements like ordering, timing, and persistence.

items.title: Condition-Contrastive Extrapolation for On-Policy Distillation of Language Models
items.summary: This research introduces on-policy distillation (OPD) to improve student language models by training them on their own generated trajectories with supervision from a stronger teacher model.

items.title: Entertain, then Cancel: How Thinking Makes Reasoning Models Read Some and Or Literally
items.summary: This study examines how the duration of a reasoning model's 'thinking' process influences its interpretation of everyday inferences, such as the literal reading of 'some' versus 'all' in language.

items.title: FlowBudget: Training-Free Sampling-Budget Estimation for Flow Matching Models
items.summary: FlowBudget proposes a training-free method for estimating the sampling budget in continuous flow-based generative models like flow matching models, optimizing inference cost by determining the number of function evaluations (NFEs).

items.title: Expanding Attention: A Taylor-Series Route to Linear-Time Transformers with a Fixed Number of Recurrent States
items.summary: This paper presents a new approach to construct linear-time Transformers by expanding the exponential attention kernel into a truncated Taylor series, resulting in a fixed number of recurrent states independent of context length.

items.title: TurboMamba: Faster Inference, Faster Training, and Better Prediction with Lexical Memory
items.summary: Introduces TurboMamba, a new language-model architecture combining Mamba-3 and Transformer components for faster inference, training, and token prediction by processing token blocks.

items.title: Recursive Offline Distillation via Entropy Gain Sampling and Answer Mixing
items.summary: This paper proposes a recursive offline distillation method using entropy gain sampling and answer mixing to transfer reasoning chains from large language models (LLMs) to smaller models, especially when full access to the teacher model is limited.

items.title: How to Train Your Little Dragon: Teaching a Small Language Model to Construct and Refine GPU Optimization Scripts
items.summary: This research introduces a training method called 'HOW TO TRAIN YOUR LITTLE DRAGON' that teaches a small language model to construct and refine GPU optimization scripts, addressing the complex interaction of compiler transformations.

items.title: Do As I Do, Not As I Say: On-Policy Distillation Inherits the Teacher in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: This study examines on-policy distillation (OPD) and supervised fine-tuning (SFT) as strategies to improve the reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) by leveraging supervision from stronger teacher models.

items.title: Bellman-Consistent Trajectory RL for LLM Arithmetic Reasoning
items.summary: This research proposes a Bellman-consistent trajectory reinforcement learning method for LLM arithmetic reasoning, which transforms sparse terminal rewards into dense token-level signals using Trajectory Bellman Residual Minimization (TBRM).

items.title: SIEVE: Overcoming Topological Obstruction in Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning
items.summary: This work identifies and resolves a theoretical incompatibility in 3D point cloud masked autoencoding with SE(3)-equivariant networks, introducing SIEVE to overcome topological obstructions that cause models to hallucinate orientation.

items.title: Noise-Space Reward Alignment for Few-Step Generative Models
items.summary: This study investigates Noise-Space Reward Alignment as a method to steer few-step generative models towards desired properties, particularly when only black-box reward evaluations are available for training.

items.title: Representation Redistribution in Sparse Autoencoders
items.summary: This research examines representation redistribution in sparse autoencoders (SAEs), showing how prompt transformations can alter activity across sparse features that decompose language model activations.

items.title: Exploring the Design Space of Permutation Diffusion LLMs
items.summary: This research explores different diffusion-LLM parameterizations for permutation generation, comparing hard-assignment and soft-assignment prediction methods over shuffled candidate-index sequences.

items.title: CoTS: Competitive Token Selection for Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.summary: CoTS (Competitive Token Selection) is proposed to enhance latent reasoning in large language models by using continuous soft embeddings or hidden states to preserve alternative reasoning paths beyond discrete Chain-of-Thought.

items.title: Reference-Guided Turn-Taking Style Transfer for Full-Duplex Spoken Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces a reference-guided approach for turn-taking style transfer in full-duplex spoken language models, allowing for adaptable conversational personalities rather than a fixed one.

items.title: Verdict: Encode Once, Decide Many
items.summary: Verdict introduces an open typed-decision model designed to automate organizational work by efficiently answering many small, probabilistic questions about a piece of state, akin to a cross-encoder.

items.title: Wolof-Adapted Industry-Ready Open-Weight Language Models
items.summary: This paper presents new 0.6B-14B open-weight language models adapted for Wolof through instruction tuning, addressing the weak support for the language in existing models and offering a cost-effective alternative to API models.

items.title: CoTranslator: Reverse to Forward Chain-of-Thought Translator for Reasoning Distillation
items.summary: CoTranslator is a method that translates reverse to forward Chain-of-Thought to facilitate reasoning distillation, aiming to efficiently obtain verified CoT data for training large language models.

items.title: Blame Errant Words, Not the Canvas: Defect-Aware Spatial Credit Assignment for Visual Text Generation
items.summary: This research introduces Defect-Aware Spatial Credit Assignment to improve visual text generation by addressing issues like incorrect wording and malformed glyphs in generated images. It identifies limitations in current recognition-based rewards and whole-image scalar feedback.

items.title: RIGen: Beyond Action Following with Reciprocal Interaction in Generative Gameplay
items.summary: RIGen explores reciprocal interaction in generative gameplay, aiming for generated worlds where player actions have persistent consequences and the world responds according to its own rules. This goes beyond simple action-following in generative video systems.

items.title: Intern Lumina U2: A Multi-Codebook Diffusion Large Language Model for Omni-Visual Understanding and Image Generation
items.summary: Intern Lumina U2 is introduced as a multi-codebook diffusion large language model designed for omni-visual understanding and image generation. It aims to unify discrete, continuous, and hybrid multimodal generation paradigms by enhancing representational capacity.

items.title: MARS - A foundational map auto-regressor
items.summary: MARS is presented as a foundational map auto-regressor specifically designed to handle the challenges of map generation from extensive non-structural vectorized data. It aims to improve upon conventional multi-stage pixel-wise generative models.

items.title: Sparse Attention for Video Generation Acceleration via Growing Sparsity and Reduced Search
items.summary: This research proposes a sparse attention method to accelerate video generation using Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) by reducing their high inference cost. The technique involves growing sparsity and reduced search to mitigate the quadratic complexity of self-attention.

items.title: UltraDiff: Transferring High-Fidelity Priors to Compressed Latent Spaces for High-Resolution Image Generation

items.title: One-Step Text Generation by Seq-Drifting
items.summary: This paper introduces Seq-Drifting, a framework designed to enable diffusion language models to generate entire text sequences in a single forward pass, addressing the multiple sampling steps typically required for high-quality text.

items.title: SWEAR: Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning via Self-Rated Difficulty
items.summary: This paper introduces SWEAR (Section-Wise Efficient Audio Reasoning), a method for large audio-language models to achieve adaptive and efficient reasoning by incorporating self-rated difficulty for granular effort estimation.

items.title: Kairos: Toward a Byte-Level Foundation Model for Every Modality
items.summary: This research introduces 'Kairos,' a byte-level foundation model designed for every modality, featuring a novel architecture combining bidirectional gated-DeltaNet linear attention and sliding-window attention for small language models.

items.title: An Input-Dependent Readout Phase for Resonant Sequence Models
items.summary: This paper proposes an input-dependent readout phase for resonant sequence models, allowing content-dependent memory while avoiding the quadratic cost of attention. It explores trade-offs between training efficiency and memory capabilities in these models.

items.title: CacheScope: Exact-Compute Allocation for Training-Free Diffusion Acceleration
items.summary: CacheScope introduces a training-free method for accelerating diffusion transformer inference by optimally allocating compute resources to replace full denoising steps with cached approximations. The approach focuses on improving efficiency through feature reuse in diffusion models.

items.title: Transformer-Based Masked Diffusion Models Provably Learn Distributions with Latent Structure
items.summary: This paper provides theoretical proof that transformer-based masked diffusion models (MDMs) can learn distributions with latent structure, generating discrete data by iteratively unmasking tokens in parallel. It also analyzes the parallelization and estimation errors inherent in these models.

items.title: DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models
items.summary: DiffusionART proposes an efficient, stable, and scalable online reinforcement learning method for fine-tuning diffusion models using black-box rewards. It aims to overcome limitations in efficiency and stability found in existing RL approaches for diffusion models.

items.title: STAPLE: Static Sparse Upcycling of Pretrained Checkpoints via Embedding Modules
items.summary: STAPLE introduces a static sparse upcycling method for pretrained LLM checkpoints using embedding modules, designed to scale parametric capacity without increasing active computation. It addresses the challenges of expensive pretraining for sparse architectures, particularly beyond Mixture-of-Experts models.

items.title: Byzantine-Resilient Federated Large Language Model via Hypergraph Message Passing
items.summary: This paper introduces a new method to make Federated Large Language Models (FedLLMs) resilient to Byzantine attacks during decentralized training, which can corrupt semantic consistency and factual accuracy.

items.title: HART: Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time series Foundation Model
items.summary: This paper introduces HART, a Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time Series Foundation Model designed for non-autoregressive multi-step forecasting, addressing long-horizon degradation seen in models like RWKV-7.

items.title: Unsupervised Multimodal Reward Modeling
items.summary: This paper describes an unsupervised method for training vision-language reward models without human preference labels, using a linear head on a frozen Qwen3-VL backbone.

items.title: COFFEQA: Counterfactual-Guided Few-Shot Distillation for LLM Question Answering
items.summary: This paper introduces COFFEQA, a counterfactual-guided few-shot distillation method aimed at training smaller, more efficient student LLMs for question answering tasks.

items.title: Time Delay System for Sequence Modeling
items.summary: This research proposes a 'Time Delay System' as a novel approach for sequence modeling to provide explicit, interpretable content-aware temporal recall, addressing limitations in current models.

items.title: Rethinking the Roles of Diffusion and Decoding: Predictive-State Flows for Parallel Language Generation
items.summary: This research rethinks the roles of diffusion and decoding in continuous diffusion language models, proposing 'Predictive-State Flows' for parallel language generation.

items.title: Surfing the Activation Wave: Analyzing the Information and Geometry of LLM Hidden States for Speculative Decoding
items.summary: This research analyzes the information and geometry of LLM hidden states to improve speculative decoding methods by optimally selecting layers for faster inference.

items.title: What Should SFT Learn? Conditional Information Gain for Generalizable Post-Training
items.summary: This paper explores what supervised fine-tuning (SFT) should learn for generalizable post-training of large language models, proposing Conditional Information Gain as a criterion.

items.title: RAMP: Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision for Efficient Prefill in Recurrent-Depth Language Models
items.summary: This paper introduces RAMP, a Recurrent Adaptive Mixed Precision technique designed to improve the efficiency of prefill operations in recurrent-depth language models, especially for long contexts.

items.title: From 2.1M Hours of Raw Broadcast Audio to Finnish Speech SSL: Confidence Filtering and Architectural Analysis at Scale
items.summary: This research details a method for creating Finnish speech self-supervised learning models from 2.1 million hours of raw broadcast audio using confidence filtering and architectural analysis.

items.title: Neurograf v1: An End-to-End Romanian-First Language Model Family

items.title: ForcingBooster: Adaptive Patch-wise Denoising for Fast Autoregressive Video Diffusion
items.summary: ForcingBooster is presented as a method for adaptive patch-wise denoising, designed to enable faster and more efficient autoregressive video diffusion for real-time interactive video generation.

items.title: Zebra3D: Efficient Hybrid Foundation Models For Scalable 3D Reconstruction
items.summary: Zebra3D introduces an efficient hybrid foundation model and a layerwise sparse-linear hybrid attention framework to improve the scalability and efficiency of pretrained 3D foundation models for large-scale 3D reconstruction.

items.title: APEX: Asynchronous Prefix Denoising for Extreme Compression
items.summary: APEX, short for Asynchronous Prefix Denoising for EXtreme compression, is introduced as a hierarchical method to achieve cheaper diffusion by aggressively compressing latent tokens in generative models while managing the reconstruction-generation dilemma.

items.title: UniMergeTrack: Hierarchical Model Merging for General RGB-X Visual Object Tracking
items.summary: UniMergeTrack introduces a hierarchical model merging approach for general RGB-X visual object tracking, aiming to improve robustness using complementary modalities like thermal infrared, event, or depth.

items.title: A4-MR: Abnormality-aware Anatomical Alignment for MR

items.summary: CompactSplat introduces a spatially adaptive Gaussian distribution approach for feedforward scene reconstruction, aiming to improve accuracy in recovering geometry and textures from sparse views.

items.summary: This paper introduces a method for generative inbetweening that uses destination-conditioned adaptation with semantic-geometric alignment to synthesize temporally coherent intermediate frames between a start and target frame.

items.title: SkillNEO: Non-Elitist Evolutionary Optimization of Agent Skills
items.summary: Agent skills turn procedural knowledge into reusable artifacts, allowing LLM agents to accumulate and refine expertise through experience. Building on this, skill evolution iteratively improves skills using execution feedback. However, improvement may require several interdependent edits, so low-reward versions can still be worth developing. Requiring immediate reward gains can discard useful partial repairs before their benefits emerge. Non-elitist evolution allows new versions to receive further edits despite scoring below earlier ones. For agent skills, this calls for evidence of what to preserve and repair next. We introduce SkillNEO (Non-Elitist Evolutionary Optimization for Agent Skills), which separately selects a version to use and versions to keep improving. Comparing how related versions perform the same task reveals working steps to preserve and remaining failures to fix. It can also revisit and revise earlier versions using later evidence. Across 86 SkillsBench tasks in eight domains, including software engineering and office work, SkillNEO raises GPT-5.4 Mini's average reward from 49.1% to 66.4%, within GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 Luna's original-skill range. Mini executes tasks, proposes revisions, and edits skills; final evaluation uses the same task instances. Gains span all eight domains. The same skills improve stronger models without further editing. On the 41 tasks with modified skills, reuse improves Luna by 10.5 percentage points and places GPT-5.5 10.6 points above its published original-skill reference. Execution records show these skills can benefit stronger models even when Mini still fails some task requirements. Search histories also show lower-scoring versions leading to skills ultimately selected for use. Together, these findings show that skill evolution can turn a weaker model's partial progress into reusable procedural knowledge for improving more capable agents.

items.title: MAI-Gym: An Open All-in-One Platform for GUI Agent Evaluation and RL Training across Mobile and Computer Environments
items.summary: Online reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiable rewards has driven rapid progress in mathematics, coding, and tool use, but scaling this success to GUI agents remains challenging due to the high cost of interactive environments and the scarcity of realistic training tasks. We introduce MAI-Gym, an open all-in-one platform that unifies GUI agent evaluation, data collection, and online RL training across mobile, computer, and web environments. Through a shared rollout pipeline, MAI-Gym ensures consistent agent behavior across evaluation and training, supports ten established benchmarks, and scales to 20,000 parallel environment instances. Beyond scalable infrastructure, MAI-Gym enables automated synthesis of diverse GUI applications and challenging tasks, including resettable mocked apps and coherent cross-app worlds with execution-validated task verifiers. Using MAI-Gym, we train MAI-Gym-9B, a unified 9B agent for mobile and computer use, achieving state-of-the-art performance among open GUI agents under 10B parameters: 78.4% on MobileWorld and 76.2% on OSWorld-Verified. Importantly, RL in a mocked train-ticketing app transfers to its real-world counterpart, improving task success on a phys- ical phone from 28.8% to 48.1%. We release the framework, synthesis skills, mocked apps, 2,000 verified tasks, and the model checkpoint to support repro- ducible research and further advances in scalable GUI agent training.

items.title: LEV: Thinking Fast and Deep with Looped Decision Models
items.summary: Decision models answer typed questions about an input with one probability per option, computed in a single forward pass without generating text. Like the fast System 1 of dual-process theory, they answer at once, but their depth is fixed at training time, so they spend the same computation on easy and hard questions. Models that reason in generated text can think longer, but they pay for every extra step in decoded tokens. We present LEV, a decision model that thinks deeper by rerunning its layers in a loop instead of generating tokens. LEV builds on a language model pretrained as a loop, reads the options after every loop step and trains all steps jointly, so one checkpoint can answer at any depth. On three looped backbones, accuracy rises with depth on the same weights, mostly on hard questions, and a 2.6B LEV goes from 63.2% at depth one to 76.2% at depth four on JevBench. On-demand depth, set per question by a small stopper with a threshold fitted on unlabelled requests, saves 15% to 24% of the computation at a cost of under one accuracy point, level with or slightly above a fixed mix of depths. On a locked test set, the 1.4B and 3B models are 5.4 to 8.8 points more accurate than dense (non-looped) models and cascades of the same latency below 50 ms.

items.title: StepSafe: Learning Timely Intervention with Context-Aware Safety Reasoning
items.summary: Safety in agentic systems is inherently sequential: whether an action is safe depends on prior actions, tool outputs, information disclosures, and interactions among agents. Recent work has shifted agent safety guardrails from post-hoc trajectory-level assessment toward step-level action diagnosis and proactive risk prediction, yet existing training objectives provide limited supervision for how step evidence accumulates over time and when it becomes sufficient to justify intervention. We propose \methodlong~(ASPO): a training framework for step-level timely intervention. Pre-fix level stage alignment allows crediting each decision at its own step: it compares each response with the other responses sampled at the same prefix and rewards the action that fits the stage, continuing before the risk is visible, asking while clarification can still avert harm, and stopping before harm is irreversible. Adaptive feedback self-distillation further credits the reasoning behind each decision, with the model itself as a teacher that sees the step annotations on intervention steps and rules mined from its own false alarms on safe steps. Its training data carry a violation taxonomy and an intervention window at every step and are extended through self-evolving multi-agent red-teaming. Finally we present \textsc{StepSafe}, a step-level reasoning guardrail with timely intervention, that achieves the state-of-the-art peformance among open-source guardrails across five agent-safety benchmarks on safety-utility pareto curve with Youden's $J$ of 53.0 (4B) against 46.2.

items.title: MSP: Modality Self-Play for Training Multimodal LLMs Without Paired Cross-Modal Data
items.summary: Large multimodal models have achieved remarkable progress by scaling model capacity and training on massive paired multimodal data. However, this paradigm introduces a fundamental bottleneck: aligned multimodal datasets are expensive to curate, difficult to scale across diverse modality combinations, and increasingly constrain further progress. We introduce Modality Self-Play (MSP), a training framework for multimodal foundation models based on proxy-mediated modality composition. Instead of relying on paired cross-modal data, MSP uses anchor-supporting proxy textual descriptions of unseen modalities as semantic bridges during training. Given an observed modality (e.g., image or audio), the model generates proxy descriptions for complementary unseen modalities, which are then encoded and aligned with the observed modality through learned bridges, enabling cross-modal interaction without real paired non-text supervision. Our central hypothesis is that proxy text, combined with contrastively trained pretrained encoders, provides sufficient semantic structure for multimodal composition to emerge. We show that MSP enables zero-shot modality composition: models trained only with a real anchor modality and accompanying proxy descriptions can integrate and reason over multiple modalities at inference time despite never observing real paired non-text data during training. Empirically, MSP achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on multiple multimodal benchmarks. Ablation studies further demonstrate that learned bridges improve alignment, while anchor-supporting proxy descriptions enable effective cross-modal composition. MSP removes the need for real paired non-text (e.g., audio-vision) supervision, while continuing to rely on modality-text pairs, pretrained contrastive encoders, and modality-distribution bridge calibration.

items.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for HPC Job Scheduling: A Statistical Evaluation
items.summary: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) offers learned job selection for High-Performance Computing (HPC), but performance against heuristics alone does not establish value beyond action masking. Six DRL treatments are compared: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Advantage Actor-Critic (A2C), and Deep Q-Network (DQN), each with and without masking. Three heuristics and a seed-paired masked uniform random control provide baselines across ten seeds on two real Slurm (Simple Linux Utility for Resource Management) workload traces, one homogeneous and one heterogeneous, under a common non-parametric framework. All masked treatments complete evaluation, whereas unmasked treatments are truncated. On the homogeneous trace, no masked DRL treatment significantly improves average waiting time or average and maximum bounded slowdown over the control. On the heterogeneous trace, MaskablePPO improves all three metrics relative to the control. Its average waiting time is equivalent to that of the three heuristics within a 10% margin, and its maximum bounded slowdown is 22% lower than that of Last-Come, First-Served (LCFS). MaskablePPO has the leading average waiting-time rank among complete treatments on both traces, but Nemenyi comparisons detect no significant difference from MaskableA2C. Among masked variants, MaskablePPO has the lowest recorded mean training time, while MaskableDQN has the lowest mean decision latency. These findings distinguish completion from baseline-specific scheduling gains and support including a masked random control when assessing the value of learned selection.

items.title: Failure Is the Mother of Success: Recovering Supervision with Grounding Hindsight
items.summary: When every rollout for a problem fails, GRPO receives neither a successful exemplar nor a nonzero group-relative advantage, so it learns nothing from exactly the problems it most needs to learn. The failed reasoning can nevertheless suggest what to try next. We present Replay-Selected Hindsight Distillation (RSHD), which turns failed attempts into an additional, tested source of supervision during GRPO training. The policy writes a corrective note about each failed attempt without seeing a reference answer or solution, then re-solves the problem with the note in context. A note is admitted only if its replays succeed more often than the original group did, after screening for notes that state the answer, and an admitted replay is distilled into the plain-prompt policy. Because admission is decided by fresh successes rather than by the failed rollout itself, the procedure can recover supervision from groups in which every attempt failed, and it applies equally to failures in mixed groups. Only the policy is trained, the only judge is the outcome verifier, and deployment requires no notes or extra inference. Across model families and sizes and two training domains, RSHD consistently improves over GRPO on in-domain benchmarks, and the gains carry over to out-of-domain evaluation sets.

items.title: Recursive Reward Improvement via Adversarial Meta-Prompt Evolution
items.summary: Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) has gained wide attention for its ability to work with limited data. In a proposer-solver loop, a proposer model writes training tasks and a solver model learns to solve them through reinforcement learning. Such loops have succeeded in mathematics and coding, where every answer can be checked automatically. Open-ended expert tasks, like clinical report generations, have no answer key, which makes simple question-answer generation not viable. Here the proposer must also write a rubric that lists the content an answer should include and the errors it should avoid. However, the unique challenge behind model-written rubric is the comprehensiveness of it. For naively generated rubric, solvers tend to exploit it, naming the expected topics without the substance behind them, which corrupts the learning process. To solve this problem, we introduce RRI, Recursive Reward Improvement, which uses a reward hacking adversary to supervise the reward. Before the solver trains on a generated task, an adversary writes an answer that games its rubric while being as useless as possible, the same model writes an honest answer without seeing the rubric, and up to two repair steps revise the rubric to make the honest answer win. The exploits found also rewrite how future tasks and rubrics are generated. On HealthBench Professional, RRI improves the adjusted score over the Generation Only self-improvement baseline by 10.9 points at 9B and 12.4 at 27B, and by 10.3 points without any external model. In particular, the gains are largest on difficult and writing tasks. We show that the 27B model trained on the HealthBench Professional description improves by 6.6 points on PRBench Hard and 8.0 on ProfBench without seeing a task from either. We further analyze the exploitable points of model-generated question-rubric pairs to facilitate future research on open-ended self-play.

items.title: Learning When to Withdraw: Curriculum Coverage and Rule-Specific Failures in Fine-Tuned Language Agents
items.summary: Tool-using language agents must revise prepared actions when evidence changes or authority is revoked. Selective withdrawal means suspending affected actions, preserving supported work, and resuming only after sufficient repair. We study supervised fine-tuning in NAQD-Env, a synthetic environment with explicit dependencies and a deterministic reference policy. Four LoRA checkpoints of Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct compare an original curriculum with an enriched one, the latter under three system-prompt framings with identical views and targets. Three instruction-tuned baselines and all four checkpoints are evaluated under three inference prompts on fresh validation cases, held-out dependency families, and held-out structural combinations. Under the naqd prompt, SFT checkpoints reach decision agreement of 0.77-0.92 and withdrawal recall of 0.46-0.86, versus 0.45-0.63 and at most 0.06 for the baselines. Rule-level diagnostics qualify these gains. The original-curriculum checkpoint wrongly withdraws 26 of 34 actions with surviving alternative support; enriched checkpoints withdraw 0-1. Conversely, all SFT checkpoints narrow prohibited combinations less often than the 7B and 8B baselines, a case absent from both curricula. Delegation results show more withdrawal but poorer preservation of independently authorized actions, and all four checkpoints omit valid event reports. Framing contrasts vary across metrics and splits and do not establish a reproducible advantage or equivalence. One training run per arm, jointly changed curriculum properties, prior evaluation exposure, and baseline-SFT quantization differences limit causal attribution. The contribution is a method for detecting rule-specific regressions that aggregate accuracy can conceal, not evidence that fine-tuning alone ensures agent safety.

items.title: Athanor: An Agent-Native System for Autonomous Post-Training Research
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement, in which AI systems build stronger AI systems, is one promising route to superintelligence. We study a weaker form that can be measured today: frontier agents post-training a small raw base model with public data, as a test of their research potential. We build Athanor, an open agent-native system for autonomous post-training research (AutoPostTrain) on real GPUs. We give the agents full research autonomy, low-friction engineering tools, and efficient starter code. The agents carry out the research themselves: they read datasets and evaluation results, build their training data, write and modify training algorithms, tune hyperparameters, and analyze the results to decide what to try next. They work in a sandbox and cannot use external teacher models. Athanor's services supply frozen evaluation, managed jobs, decontaminated data, a persistent research record, and a held-out suite the agents are unaware of. In a 104-hour campaign, a team of four Claude Opus 5.5 agents, each on an eight-GPU node and given no research advice, improves Qwen3-4B-Base from 15.9 to 67.3 on a six-task development suite and from 9.2 to 48.2 on a held-out suite, against 66.5 and 47.9 for the official Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that a team of frontier agents can autonomously post-train a raw base model into a cross-domain generalist model that matches or surpasses the official instruct version on average. The campaign's full record shows that the agents reach this level by recombining known methods and each other's models: SFT on public reasoning data, RL with a rollout change one agent introduced, weight merges across agents, and rounds of self-distillation. With execution handled, today's agents already have the engineering and research ability to conquer this task. We hope Athanor provides a foundation for scaling autonomous AI research.

items.title: OmicsBench: a long-horizon multi-turn benchmark of AI agents on research-study-scale bioinformatics
items.summary: Computational biologists increasingly delegate substantial analyses to AI agents in long-horizon, multi-turn sessions, yet most benchmarks of agents' bioinformatics capabilities pose a single short task with a single-shot prompt. We present OmicsBench, a long-horizon, multi-turn bioinformatics benchmark for AI agents. Each of its 97 tasks links dependent subtasks into a directed acyclic graph, for 662 underlying subtasks in all. Each subtask is posed as one user turn and graded deterministically against an answer key, with optional in-context feedback on incorrect answers. Across 12 models on three harnesses, the slowest agent averages 3.6 hours per task, and no combination comes near saturating the benchmark, with mean scores of 0.43 to 0.57 out of a possible 1 without in-context feedback and 0.54 to 0.67 with it. Multi-turn evaluation also uncovers behavior that single-shot prompts cannot, as agents score lower on subtasks that depend on earlier subtasks, and in-context feedback helps agents recover some of that loss. Because deterministic scoring gives no qualitative account of how an agent failed, we also introduce an unsupervised failure mode discovery pipeline that describes, embeds, and clusters agents' failed attempts to surface emergent failure modes. Applied to OmicsBench, this pipeline exposes qualitative shortcomings in how agents carry out bioinformatics analyses, ranging from agents applying their own statistical filters in place of the specified ones to agents writing whole answers from memory.

items.title: Sci$\Pi$vot: Benchmarking Principal-Investigator Judgment at Pivotal Moments of Scientific AutoResearch Agents
items.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents can keep scientific experiments running for months with little human supervision, but reliable autonomous research also requires scientific judgment. Evaluating scientific judgment is difficult because research decisions are open-ended and depend on project context. We construct Sci$\Pi$vot, a 248-case benchmark of scientific judgment based on human corrections. The benchmark draws on records from six months of research in which senior researchers ran LLM agents on 26 projects across six scientific fields and repeatedly intervened to correct the agents' research judgments. In each case, an agent chooses between the original LLM plan and the human-corrected alternative, using only the project record available before the correction as context. We compare LLM and human performance and examine the effects of reasoning effort, access to the project record, and reconsideration. At medium reasoning effort with the project record, models systematically prefer the original LLM plan over the human-corrected alternative. Four of five frontier models perform below chance on the selected cases. The highest accuracy in the project condition across the tested models and reasoning effort settings is 63.5%, compared with 73.4% for fresh researchers. At medium effort, every model achieves lower accuracy with the project record than without it, and reconsideration does not consistently improve overall accuracy. Even with a human-corrected alternative available, frontier models struggle with the selected research decisions, while Sci$\Pi$vot supports systematic evaluation of scientific judgment for LLM agents.

items.title: MemComposer: Learning to Assemble Memories for LLM Agents via Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Agent memory enables large language model (LLM) agents to reuse past experiences without updating their parameters. However, semantic similarity alone does not guarantee memory usefulness: downstream performance depends on how memories are selected and presented to the agent. We propose MemComposer, a memory composer that jointly examines the current query and retrieved candidates to decide which experiences to include, how many to select, and how to order them. We train the composer using Experience Policy Optimization (ExPO), a GRPO-based framework that evaluates assembled memory contexts through complete agent interactions and uses task-success feedback to optimize the assembly policy. Across three $\tau^2$-bench domains with two frozen executors, MemComposer outperforms the strongest baseline for each executor while reducing average memory-token usage by 16.9% and 4.9%, respectively. The learned policy also transfers to unseen domains, executors, and memory banks, and benefits from memories generated by stronger models without further training. These results demonstrate the value of learning query-specific memory assembly using downstream task feedback.

items.title: Planning Commitment of LLM under Partial Observability
items.summary: LLM-based planning agents commit to plans of different lengths before interacting with a partially observable environment. Some aggressively commit to a long plan based on assumptions about unobserved states, while others conservatively plan only over what they have observed. Both behaviors emerge implicitly in pre-trained models, whether the LLM outputs a plan directly or generates a PDDL formulation for a classical solver. Aggressive commitment risks costly failures, while conservative commitment risks excessive LLM calls. This choice pits safety against efficiency, a trade-off that has been neither characterized systematically nor made controllable. We investigate aggressive and conservative LLM planners and formalizers on two partially observable domains, where priors are provided as either explicit statistics or common-sense knowledge. Across three LLMs, both strategies reach similar accuracy. Conservative methods achieve fewer failed attempts (safety) at the cost of more API calls (efficiency). Aggressive methods fail more often but replan efficiently only when priors are informative. Interestingly, analysis shows that LLMs treat the provided priors nearly as facts, which risks failure when priors are unreliable. We also explore hybrid strategies with tunable hyperparameters that adjust the balance between safety and efficiency.

items.title: Kolab: Benchmarking Human-Agent Collaboration in Long-Horizon Workflows
items.summary: When humans collaborate with AI agents on long-horizon tasks, what happens to the agents' contributions? For solving long-horizon tasks, humans place greater importance on ongoing interaction with AI agents (e.g., revising plans) than on an agent's ability to complete the task in a single attempt. However, most agentic benchmarks have focused more on automation. Strong performance on such benchmarks does not imply effective real-world collaboration. Professional workflows offer a useful setting, as they often involve interdependent steps. To address this gap, we introduce Kolab, a new dataset of 115+ hours of screen recordings of 50 professionals from 40 occupations collaborating with agents on realistic, long-horizon problems. Kolab also contains participants' collaboration and output quality judgments. Our analysis reveals diverse collaboration patterns, highlighting the importance of when and how professionals coordinate with agents. A collaborative agent must do two things that automation benchmarks never test: anticipate whether experts will adopt, modify, or reject its contribution once it leaves the chat window to guide its next steps, and assess collaboration quality from the unfolding workflow without constant expert feedback. Our benchmark operationalizes both: (1) forecasting how professionals use agent contributions at diverse workflows, and (2) verifying their judgments of collaboration satisfaction and output quality. Findings show that frontier models, both agentic and non-agentic, overestimate collaboration with experts and struggle to distinguish between high- and low-quality collaboration. Longer workflow context does not consistently improve these predictions. As frontier agents cannot yet understand long-horizon collaboration with experts, we position Kolab as a valuable dataset for studying human-agent collaboration grounded in real professional workflows.

items.title: CleanRM: Reward Modeling from Noisy Feedback with a Few Clean Feedback for RLHF
items.summary: Feedback noise is pervasive in preference data, arising from subjective human judgments, annotation mistakes, and imperfect LLM judges. Standard reward modeling trained on such feedback yields a biased estimate of the clean risk. Although classical denoising methods are directly applicable to noisy feedback learning, they generally assume a uniform noise ratio across samples. However, this assumption fails for feedback data, where noise is intrinsically sample-wise. To address this challenge, we propose CleanRM, which uses a few clean feedback to calibrate sample-wise noise ratios via optimal transport. Specifically, CleanRM aligns the joint distribution of preferences reverted from noisy feedback with that of clean feedback and then trains the reward model using a noise-corrected surrogate loss. Theoretically, we prove that the resulting objective is unbiased with respect to the clean risk. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CleanRM outperforms state-of-the-art denoising baselines and yields more effective downstream RLHF alignment.

items.title: All-in-One Memory: Process-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Memory Agents
items.summary: Large language models increasingly rely on external memory to answer queries grounded in long-horizon histories such as multi-session dialogues and lengthy documents. However, existing memory methods often optimize retrieval and memory construction separately, without a shared reward space for evaluating search, writing, and stopping decisions. To address this, we propose All-in-One Memory (AiO-Mem), which organizes these operations as transitions over a shared evidence state and directly evaluates the semantic quality of each action in a unified reward space. AiO-Mem compiles heterogeneous histories into source-traceable multi-view events, providing a shared substrate for retrieval and memory writing. A unified memory policy actor then rolls out complete interaction trajectories over this shared evidence state. A separate trajectory-conditioned process reward model is trained through evidence-grounded supervised fine-tuning and trajectory-level DPO to assign process scores to the collected trajectories. These scores are aggregated into an action-balanced trajectory reward and used by Process-Aligned DAPO (PA-DAPO) to optimize the memory policy. Across long-context memory benchmarks, AiO-Mem consistently improves answer accuracy over both static memory systems and RL-trained memory agents.

items.title: GRADS: Graph-Regulated Agentic Data Synthesis with Controllable Difficulty
items.summary: Deep research agents are increasingly deployed to retrieve precise information from large corpora, yet multi-hop, long-horizon tasks remain challenging. Synthetic data generation has emerged as a scalable solution, with existing pipelines typically expanding seed tasks to increase their apparent depth and breadth. However, this expansion does not reliably translate into necessary reasoning: newly introduced evidence may be only weakly coupled to the answer, creating a mismatch between intended and empirical difficulty. To address this problem, we introduce GRADS, a graph-guided agentic data synthesis framework with explicit difficulty control. GRADS runs a closed loop of seed selection, evidence expansion, question--answer construction, and verification while maintaining a graph of the evidence and inference dependencies required to derive each answer. At each step, it conditions generation on a relevant subgraph, preserving indispensable inference without accumulating irrelevant context. Experiments across security, software-engineering, and scientific-document domains show that GRADS consistently generates verified tasks with empirically separated difficulty distributions, as measured by independent solvers. Moreover, under matched training budgets, post-training on this data delivers consistent gains at every level: SFT raises the solution-termination rate to over 95% while cutting tool calls and turns by up to 75%, RL trims tool use by up to a further 19.5%, and on our held-out, domain-specific benchmarks, the resulting 4B model matches Sonnet~4 on software engineering and surpasses it on the scientific and security domains.

items.title: MemScope: Evolving Agent Memory Architectures through Localized Code Repair
items.summary: Agent memory architectures define how LLM agents store and reuse experience across tasks, but they are typically fixed after deployment, limiting their adaptability across task types. Recent self-evolving approaches instead adapt these memory architectures using execution feedback, typically represented as evaluation scores or compressed summaries. However, such coarse-grained feedback is insufficient for precise failure localization in current agent systems, where long-horizon task execution involves multiple interacting components. Without a precise failure location, existing approaches lack a clear code-level target for modification, leaving the update scope weakly constrained and often leading to large-scale rewrites of an otherwise capable memory architecture. We propose MemScope, a framework for evidence-grounded, localized evolution of an existing memory architecture. Its tool-using Patch Agent jointly inspects raw execution traces, runtime memory state, and current architecture code to identify repair targets and apply bounded, in-place edits under provider-identity and memory-compatibility constraints. On GAIA, the trace-and-memory inspection variant achieves 86.67% accuracy, compared with 70.00% for trace-only and 63.33% for summary-only feedback. Under xBench tasks, the evolved memory architecture improves over its original version from 49 to 55 correct answers with DeepSeek V3.2 and from 50 to 53 with Kimi K2.7 Code. On disjoint ALFWorld unseen tasks, success rises from 50.75% to 71.64%. Across archived architecture-snapshot transitions, the median code-change ratio is 4.4%. These results support fine-grained execution evidence as a basis for localized, in-place memory-architecture evolution.

items.title: Mine, Sample, Render: Test-Time Diversity Alignment Of Generative Models
items.summary: Modern generative models produce high-quality individual outputs but struggle to sample diversely, even when explicitly instructed to do so. We introduce MINE-SAMPLE-RENDER (MSR), a test-time approach that externalizes the diversity into an explicit, corpus-derived sampling procedure. Our pipeline (i) mines an interpretable categorical schema from a corpus of real artifacts and supplies statistics for sampling; (ii) samples attribute configurations from the corpus-derived statistics; (iii) uses a generative model purely as a conditional renderer of a sampled configuration. Across weather report generation, user simulation, webpage design, text-to-image generation, and agent-generated 3D assets, we evaluate the diversity and output quality of MSR-guided generation and show that MSR improves alignment with corpus distributions and diversity of generated outputs.

items.title: The Density of Thought: Predicting and Steering Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.summary: This research investigates the information density within chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning steps in large language models to predict answer correctness and explore it as a controllable target during inference.

items.title: Quantum Versus Classical Machine Learning for Neuropsychiatric Disorders: A Feature-Matched Multi-Cohort Evaluation
items.summary: This study conducts a feature-matched multi-cohort evaluation comparing quantum and classical machine learning models for classifying neuropsychiatric disorders using resting-state functional connectivity data.

items.title: KNOU-Flood: Advancing global streamflow forecasting with lead-aware probabilistic machine learning
items.summary: KNOU-Flood advances global streamflow forecasting for flood preparedness by using lead-aware probabilistic machine learning, addressing the skill degradation of data-driven models when driven by operational forecasts.

items.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility
items.summary: This research investigates the data requirements for training Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs), examining how much activation data is necessary and whether functional behavior guarantees feature reproducibility across different data scales.

items.title: On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: Discusses on-policy residual learning for Diffusion Language Models, highlighting the importance and challenges of using residual context to improve the speed-quality trade-off in these models.

items.title: Quantile-Guided Diffusion for Probabilistic Time-Series Forecasting
items.summary: Introduces a method for probabilistic time-series forecasting by using predicted quantiles to control the distributional output of diffusion forecasters.

items.title: Optimal Hydra: Model Heterogeneous Federated Learning for LLMs using Data-Informed Hydra-Nets
items.summary: Introduces Optimal Hydra, a method for model heterogeneous federated learning for LLMs that uses data-informed Hydra-Nets to enable efficient training on decentralized private data.

items.title: Semantic Alignment of EEG and Text: A Contrastive Learning Framework for Decoding Imagined Speech
items.summary: Proposes a contrastive learning framework for semantically aligning EEG signals with text to decode imagined speech, aiming to advance naturalistic brain-computer interfaces.

items.title: EEG-Based Prediction of Music Enjoyment Using Deep Learning with Explainable Temporal Analysis
items.summary: Utilizes deep learning and explainable temporal analysis on EEG data to predict music enjoyment, aiming to understand neural responses to music.

items.title: Optimal Explicit and Implicit Regularization Strengths in High-Dimensional Continual Linear Regression
items.summary: Studies continual linear regression in a high-dimensional setting, deriving a closed-form expression for the generalization loss of a model trained with gradient descent.

items.title: Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization for Off-Policy RL with Verifiable Rewards
items.summary: Introduces Gibbs-Gap Policy Optimization, a new method for off-policy reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, designed to reduce variance when training language models on responses from different behavior policies.

items.title: Task-Phase-Conditioned Expert Routing Is Not a Reliable Proxy for Quantization Sensitivity in MoE FFN Tensors
items.summary: Investigates whether expert routing statistics in Mixture-of-Experts language models reliably indicate quantization sensitivity for layer-wise mixed-precision quantization of FFN tensors.

items.title: Amortizing Sequential Experimental Design in Reasoning LLMs
items.summary: Studies how to amortize sequential Bayesian experimental design into reasoning LLMs by explicitly training them to adaptively gather information for experimental design tasks.

items.title: Denoising Score Matching in Diffusion Models: The Effect of Rank Constraints on Generalization
items.summary: Studies the effect of rank constraints on generalization in denoising score matching within diffusion models, exploring how architectural biases influence the functions score networks can represent.

items.title: Long-Context Drafting Does Not Require Long-Context Drafters
items.summary: Investigates speculative decoding in ultra-long context scenarios, arguing that long-context drafters are not always necessary as their cost can erode and reverse the intended speedup.

items.title: Clinically Interpretable Biological Age Estimation Using CatBoost and SHAP with Continuous and Categorical Features from NHANES
items.summary: Develops a clinically interpretable machine learning model using CatBoost and SHAP to estimate biological age from continuous and categorical features derived from NHANES data.

items.title: CogDrift-4D: Hierarchical Multimodal Modeling of Temporal Behavioral Decay for MCI Detection
items.summary: Introduces CogDrift-4D, a hierarchical multimodal modeling approach for detecting mild cognitive impairment by capturing subtle temporal behavioral decay, alongside a new behavioral dataset.

items.title: Wrong Votes, Right Gradients: Why Majority-Vote Rewards Track Verifiable RL
items.summary: Explores why majority-vote rewards are effective in reinforcement learning, explaining how they track verifiable RL and influence gradients despite their seemingly simple mechanism.

items.title: Sign Betting for Misspecified Regression: Variance Adaptivity and Optimal Approximation
items.summary: This item explores a theoretical machine learning approach for bounded regression under model misspecification, using an L1 distance metric relevant for downstream decision problems like bandits and reinforcement learning.

items.title: Task-Centric Multimodal Learning for Cognitive Impairment Detection
items.summary: This research focuses on using task-centric multimodal learning to improve the early detection of cognitive impairment, addressing the limitations of traditional text or voice-based models in capturing the full scope of human cognition.

items.title: SALTO: Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators for Nonlinear Event Inference
items.summary: This paper presents SALTO (Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators), a method to address the unreliability of sensitivities in learned dynamical models when differentiated, enhancing their utility in inverse problems and scientific decision-making.

items.title: StochLOB: Heavy-Tailed Score Matching for Robust Limit Order Book Trend Prediction
items.summary: StochLOB introduces a heavy-tailed score matching technique for robust limit order book trend prediction, improving upon traditional score-based diffusion methods that often use Gaussian noise poorly suited for bursty market time series.

items.title: Predicting Live Birth After Fresh Embryo Transfer in IVF/ICSI: Differential ICM/Trophectoderm Morphology Encoding and a Hybrid Attention--Logistic Regression Ensemble
items.summary: This research develops a predictive model using differential ICM/trophectoderm morphology encoding and a hybrid attention-logistic regression ensemble to forecast live birth outcomes after fresh embryo transfer in IVF/ICSI.

items.title: Language Models Share a Readout Bottleneck in Working Memory
items.summary: This study finds that large language models (LLMs) exhibit a working memory signature similar to humans on the N-back task, showing performance decline with increased memory load and concentrated errors on specific lure items.

items.title: Judging the Judges: Confidence and Disagreement in Rubrics as Rewards
items.summary: This paper explores 'Rubrics as Rewards' (RaR), a method extending reinforcement learning to non-verifiable domains by using an LLM judge to score responses against a structured rubric, focusing on confidence and disagreement in these judgments.

items.title: Hard Way, The Only Way: Provable Merits of Training on Hardest Examples
items.summary: This theoretical work provides a high-dimensional theory explaining the merits of training AI systems on the hardest examples, offering a unified understanding of data pruning's effectiveness.

items.title: A Large-Scale Dataset for Multi-Class Financial News Classification in Brazilian Portuguese
items.summary: This paper introduces a large-scale dataset of approximately 160,000 Brazilian Portuguese financial news articles to address the scarcity of domain-specific resources for Financial NLP systems.

items.title: Real-time Chatbot Romance Scam Detection in Stage Classification
items.summary: This study developed a real-time chatbot using the Line Messaging API to detect romance scams by classifying stages based on social science theories.

items.title: MeddeX: A Retrieval-Augmented LLaMA-3 System with Gemini Vision for Evidence-Backed Medical Report Analysis
items.summary: MeddeX is a retrieval-augmented system combining a QLoRA fine-tuned LLaMA-3 and Gemini Vision to analyze medical reports for evidence-backed insights, aiming to reduce the burden on clinical professionals.

items.title: Can LLMs Anticipate Their Cruxes?
items.summary: This paper explores methods for language models to anticipate and explain the crucial parts of their reasoning, aiming to make their decision-making process more understandable and practical for human users.

items.title: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
items.summary: This research paper investigates the dynamics of the unembedding matrix during language model pretraining, analyzing how it evolves and impacts the acquisition of model capabilities.

items.title: Multimodal AI Detection for Math-Heavy Scientific Text
items.summary: This research explores multimodal AI detection methods for identifying AI-generated content in math-heavy scientific texts, aiming to increase transparency in academic writing.

items.title: A Jury, Not an Electorate: Label-Free Reliability Estimation for Ensembles of Language Models
items.summary: This paper proposes a method for label-free reliability estimation for ensembles of language models, viewing them as a "jury" where credibility is assessed rather than simple majority.

items.title: CoSTA: Compressed Speech Token Adaptation for Efficient Spoken Dialogue Models
items.summary: CoSTA (Compressed Speech Token Adaptation) is proposed as a method to improve the efficiency of Spoken Dialogue Models by optimizing speech tokenization to reduce sequence length and inference costs.

items.title: From Observation to Intervention: Distilling Self-Generated In-Context Demonstrations via Executable Causal Intervention
items.summary: This research explores a method for distilling self-generated in-context demonstrations for LLMs using executable causal intervention, aiming to improve the quality of few-shot learning by focusing on causal rationales.

items.title: Automatic Sentence Completion Using Bengali Audio Speech with a Transformer-Based Early Speech Recognition System
items.summary: This research describes an application of a transformer-based early speech recognition system for automatic sentence completion using Bengali audio, designed to assist individuals with dementia in communication.

items.title: What Should We Remove? Evaluating the Reliability and Costs of RLVR Data Decontamination
items.summary: This research evaluates the reliability and data-loss costs associated with data decontamination policies for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) math corpora, particularly concerning benchmark overlap.

items.title: FGSS-BO: Feedback-Guided Hypothesis Management for LLM-Based Bayesian Optimization
items.summary: This research proposes FGSS-BO (Feedback-Guided Search State for Bayesian Optimization), a structured hypothesis-management interface designed to improve LLM-guided Bayesian optimization through explicit language-based feedback.

items.title: LLM-Based Weak Annotation for Cybersecurity Tweet Classification: A Teacher-Student Framework
items.summary: This research presents an LLM-based weak annotation approach within a teacher-student framework for classifying cybersecurity-related tweets to enhance cyber threat intelligence.

items.title: Making every stage of medical device document assessment with large language models deterministic
items.summary: This research explores using large language models to automate and make deterministic the assessment process for medical device documentation, aiming to streamline compliance verification.

items.title: Hybrid Generative-Tagging Decoding for Efficient Product Attribute-Value Extraction
items.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid generative-tagging decoding method for efficient product attribute-value extraction, a crucial task for building high-quality e-commerce product catalogs. It combines generative and tagging strategies to extract attribute names and their corresponding values.

items.title: Emotion Is Not External Knowledge: Internal Attention Signals for Affective State Reasoning
items.summary: This research explores how Large Language Models (LLMs) infer affective states from sparse contextual cues in multi-turn interactions by analyzing their internal attention signals. It aims to understand how LLMs maintain latent conversational states beyond explicit facts.

items.title: RenoLayout: Unified Floorplan Renovation and Furniture Layout for Constraint-Aware Residential Design
items.summary: RenoLayout proposes a unified approach for floorplan renovation and furniture layout in residential design, enabling constraint-aware transformations of existing homes. Unlike previous methods, it accounts for existing building boundaries and diverse design preferences.

items.title: ESG-Kor: A Korean Dataset for ESG-related Information Extraction and Practical Use Cases
items.summary: ESG-Kor is a new Korean dataset designed for automatically extracting Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information, addressing the growing need for specialized datasets for pre-trained language models. The dataset supports practical use cases in ESG analysis.

items.title: DPA-MoE: A Runtime Precision Control Framework for MoE Inference
items.summary: DPA-MoE introduces a runtime precision control framework for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference, allowing selected experts to operate at any precision. This framework encodes expert feed-forward weights to enhance computational efficiency.

items.title: Calibration Language Shapes Block-Influence Pruning in Multilingual Language Models
items.summary: This research investigates how the choice of calibration language impacts Block Influence (BI) pruning in multilingual language models, specifically examining its transferability from English to Indian languages in models like Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B, and Gemma-2-2B.

items.title: Beyond Invariance: Factor-wise Selective Treatment of Shifts for Multimodal Learning
items.summary: This paper proposes a factor-wise selective treatment of distribution shifts for robust multimodal learning, moving beyond uniform invariance approaches. It aims to improve robustness by distinguishing and differentially treating various types of shifted information.

items.title: Identifying Effective Strategies in Prompt Evolution for Stress and Emotion Prediction
items.summary: This research identifies effective strategies for prompt evolution to improve stress and emotion prediction using large language models from social media data. It investigates how prompt revisions impact prediction accuracy and the consistency of gains.

items.title: HyCo: Hybrid Drafting for Cost-Efficient Mobile-Cloud Speculative Decoding
items.summary: HyCo introduces a hybrid drafting method for cost-efficient mobile-cloud speculative decoding, assigning prediction depth to the server model's native multi-token prediction (MTP) head. This approach reduces repeated passes on the mobile neural processing unit (NPU) with a small language model.

items.title: Translation Circuit Discovery and Targeted Optimization for Low-Resource Multilingual Translation
items.summary: This paper explores the discovery of translation circuits and targeted optimization within multilingual decoder-only LLMs to improve low-resource multilingual translation, using Hindi-to-Urdu as a case study. It investigates the internal mechanisms responsible for translation performance.

items.title: Towards automatic digital garment assembly
items.summary: This paper addresses the time-consuming process of creating digital garments by proposing methods towards automatic digital garment assembly from existing two-dimensional patterns. It aims to automate the manual definition of sewing operations and arrangement of pattern panels in garment CAD software.

items.title: WorldCast: Exploring Intelligent Visual Generation in World State Prediction
items.summary: WorldCast explores intelligent visual generation for world state prediction, leveraging multimodal generative systems to integrate observations and synthesize visual outputs depicting future changes. It aims to characterize this emerging capability of forecasting world evolution.

items.title: Purify Before You Align: Improving Representation Alignment for Diffusion Models
items.summary: This paper proposes a method to improve representation alignment for diffusion models by "purifying" features before alignment, distinguishing more useful information for generation. This enhances and accelerates diffusion training by refining matches to pretrained visual encoders.

items.title: ReasonUni: Reasoning-Augmented Reconstruction Advances Unified Multimodal Models
items.summary: ReasonUni introduces reasoning-augmented reconstruction to advance Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs), coupling image-to-text understanding and text-to-image generation. It aims to provide more comprehensive supervision beyond perception-centric methods.

items.title: Probing Negation Understanding in Vision-Language Models With Object Attention
items.summary: This research probes how Vision-Language Models (VLMs) understand negation by analyzing their object attention patterns and comparing them to human gaze. The study aims to investigate the effectiveness of VLMs in processing this fundamental aspect of language.

items.title: DefoliationCAM: An Edge-AI System for Real-Time Insect Defoliation Severity Assessment in Grapevines
items.summary: DefoliationCAM (D-CAM) is an edge AI system developed for real-time, objective assessment of insect defoliation severity in grapevines. This solar-powered system uses a YOLO pipeline to estimate canopy defoliation and transmits data to a web dashboard.

items.title: Pixels to Tokens: Token Space Efficient Active Learning for Low-Budget Semantic Segmentation
items.summary: This paper introduces token space efficient active learning for low-budget semantic segmentation, aiming to reduce annotation requirements for foundation models and vision transformers (ViTs). It addresses the high pixel labeling costs of current active learning strategies.

items.title: PiCo: Physics-Informed Concept Probing for Geo-Foundation Models
items.summary: PiCo (Physics-Informed Concept Probing) is a method for evaluating Geo-Foundation Models (GFMs) to understand which physical features they are sensitive to or use in prediction. This helps developers test hypotheses about model behavior and aids model selection.

items.title: EigDiff: Eigensample Diffusion - or how to significantly reduce training dataset size with marginal performance variation?
items.summary: EigDiff (Eigensample Diffusion) is a method aiming to significantly reduce the training dataset size for diffusion models while maintaining performance. It addresses the high cost of training diffusion models by identifying and reducing redundancies in training data.

items.title: Mind the Tail: Data Selection Through Sparse Concepts
items.summary: This research investigates data selection strategies for training models, focusing on how reallocating training support across visual concepts impacts downstream model behavior, especially for sparse "tail concepts."

items.title: Audio-Visual Dog Identification and Tracking in Real-World Videos
items.summary: This research explores methods for audio-visual identification and tracking of individual dogs in real-world videos using barks and visual cues. This application aims to enable long-term behavioral analysis and veterinary monitoring.

items.title: RoboCloth: A Large-Scale Real Cloth Material Dataset for Neural Reflectance Reconstruction
items.summary: RoboCloth is introduced as a large-scale dataset of 500 real cloth materials captured using robotically controlled camera and lighting for neural reflectance reconstruction. Each material is imaged across approximately 580 high-dynamic range frames.

items.title: Trajectory Prediction Method for person under WSN with Hierarchical Envelope Adversarial Domain Adaptation
items.summary: This paper introduces a trajectory prediction method for pedestrians using Hierarchical Envelope Adversarial Domain Adaptation under Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN). It aims to address the challenges of complex and unpredictable pedestrian interactions for applications like autonomous driving.

items.title: VisualTrust: Video Reasoning under On-Screen Claim Framing
items.summary: VisualTrust explores multimodal large language models' "claim deference" in video reasoning, studying their tendency to prioritize on-screen claims over video content. This research investigates how models process and trust textual information presented alongside video.

items.title: ControlFlow3D: Distilling Multi-View Knowledge into Latent Flow Matching for Point Cloud Upsampling
items.summary: ControlFlow3D is a proposed framework that distills multi-view knowledge into latent flow matching for point cloud upsampling. It aims to improve 3D applications by addressing challenges of sparse observations and better exploiting visual cues from multi-view images.

items.title: SpaceCache: Intermediate Feature Reuse for Efficient Semantic Segmentation on Point Cloud Streams
items.summary: SpaceCache introduces a method for efficient semantic segmentation on point cloud streams by reusing intermediate features from point-cloud transformers. This approach aims to reduce redundant computations for applications like autonomous driving and robotics.

items.title: FocusOPD: Structure-Guided On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Models
items.summary: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation enables rectified-flow models with diffusion-transformer architectures to combine task-specific capabilities within a single student. However, matching model outputs does not guarantee that their internal representations are aligned, and it remains unclear where and when additional feature supervision is most useful. We analyze the teacher-student feature mismatch across Transformer blocks and denoising timesteps, and find that the mismatch is concentrated in deeper Transformer blocks during early denoising and persists after OPD distillation, indicating ineffective distillation. Motivated by this observation, we introduce FocusOPD, which augments the base OPD objective with token-wise directional feature alignment restricted to deep layers and early denoising steps. Across two rectified-flow backbones and multiple OPD objectives, FocusOPD improves capability transfer in compositional generation, text rendering, and preference-based evaluation. On the primary benchmark, it improves over DiffusionOPD from 0.953 to 0.967 on GenEval, from 23.797 to 23.944 on PickScore, and from 6.052 to 6.199 on LAION-Aesthetic. Ablations show that selective deep and early supervision is more effective and efficient than alignment over the full network and trajectory.

items.title: Do VLAs Really Follow Instructions? Diagnosing How-Level Instruction Following in Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are expected to follow instructions like their language backbones, yet prior work has focused on What-level instructions that specify the task rather than How-level instructions that specify how to carry it out. Through our diagnoses, we find that How-level instructions do not help current VLAs and lower task success. We hypothesize that pairing each training episode with a single instruction limits How-level instruction following, and show that training with segment-level enriched instructions makes actions respond to such instructions without consistently raising task success. To measure How-level instruction following beyond standard benchmarks, we introduce SIMPLER-IN, where success requires conditions given only in the instruction. It shows that the gained responsiveness does not extend to demanding or out-of-distribution How-level instructions. How-level instruction following thus remains an open challenge.

items.title: TRACER: A Multimodal Harness for Patient Care in Hospitals
items.summary: Continuous video and clinical records provide complementary information for understanding how patient behavior evolves over a hospital stay. A central challenge is how to represent behavior across the entire stay while preserving access to fine-grained visual and clinical evidence. We introduce TRACER, a training-free multimodal harness that constructs minute-level action records from video and combines them with clinical records into hourly reports. The harness equips an LLM agent with tools to query this hierarchy, inspect relevant video, and retrieve clinical records. To evaluate TRACER, we construct two benchmarks. The first contains 397 annotated one-minute clips spanning 15 atomic actions; the second poses 144 clinician-informed multiple-choice questions, grounded in 264 hours of video and clinical records from two ICU patients. TRACER achieves up to 84.8% accuracy for action detection and 61.0% QA accuracy versus 49.3% for the strongest baseline using the same backbone. Across 280 patients spanning approximately 60,000 camera-hours, TRACER identifies significantly less purposeful activity in patients with a positive delirium assessment during their stay than in those without (p < 0.0001). Our results show that combining continuous video with clinical records can support understanding of patient behavior over time and across patient cohorts without training on protected health data.

items.title: ReState: Noise-Level-Aware State Correction for Training-Free Object Removal in Few-Step Diffusion Models
items.summary: Training-free object removal commonly redirects self-attention away from the target region, but on few-step distilled diffusion models this often leaves object-shaped residuals. We identify a temporal mismatch: a structured prediction forms inside the mask at the first forward, and the short trajectory offers few later chances to revise it, while attention rerouting acts mainly in later steps. Across four distilled backbones, magnitude-matched single-forward interventions show that background-directed state correction affects the final result more than attention rerouting. We therefore propose ReState, which corrects the masked clean prediction toward background evidence retrieved from the input using a noise-level-aware weight that vanishes at the final forward. ReState retains object-excluding attention as a complementary constraint and adds no denoiser evaluations. Across two paired benchmarks and two few-step backbones, ReState achieves the best masked PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS among training-free methods, improving PSNR by 3.17 dB on average over the strongest baseline. On OBER-Test, it also outperforms the 50-step attention-forcing reference on all three metrics at 6.7x lower latency. The same configuration transfers to two additional distilled backbones without retuning. Project page: https://tdrlee.github.io/ReState

items.title: GeoPano: Towards Geometrically Accurate 3D Reconstruction from a Single Panorama
items.summary: Panoramic 3D reconstruction enables the holistic recovery of complete 360 $^\circ$ scene geometry, offering significant benefits for robotics and AR/VR applications. However, directly estimating geometry from ERP images is inherently challenged by spherical distortions. To reduce spherical projection distortions, a common strategy is to decompose panoramas into distortion-free perspective views, but independently processing these views often introduces cross-view geometric inconsistencies. To address these challenges, we introduce GeoPano, a feed-forward framework for single-view panoramic 3D reconstruction that recovers a geometrically accurate and consistent point cloud from a single panorama. Our approach is driven by two key innovations: First, we propose a panoramic-aware attention aggregator, featuring a streamlined attention architecture equipped with a novel Pano-Attention mechanism, which explicitly exploits the intrinsic spherical geometry of the panorama to guide cross-view interactions, thereby suppressing geometric inconsistencies. Furthermore, we formulate a hybrid supervision strategy to jointly enforce fine-grained local details in perspective space and global structural coherence in spherical space. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms previous SOTA approaches in reconstruction accuracy, geometric consistency, and visual fidelity.

items.title: VLA-$\Delta$: Learning Physical State Transition for Vision-Language-Action Models
items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models transfer semantic knowledge acquired through vision-language pretraining to robot control, achieving strong performance across various benchmarks. However, most VLAs directly map observations to demonstrated actions without explicit supervision of intermediate physical state changes, making them prone to overfitting observation-action correspondences. Some methods introduce intermediate reasoning or future-state prediction in language, visual, or latent spaces to guide action generation, but do not explicitly supervise the physical state transition itself. We therefore propose VLA-$\Delta$, a general framework that uses physical changes between current and future states as explicit learning targets. To support this objective, we construct a large-scale pretraining dataset and derive physical state-transition annotations covering task-relevant semantics and visual motion changes, providing more direct supervision for continuous action generation. During inference, the model generates actions directly from current observations without additional inference overhead.
